sponsor: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
audience: Bachelor's or master's students in biology, computer science, data science, mathematics, physics, neuroscience, chemistry, or related fields.
notes: Program was paused for the 2026 cycle; check late 2026 for future cycle status.

name: CERN Summer Student Programme
audience: Bachelor's or master's students in physics, computing, engineering, mathematics, or related disciplines; all nationals may apply, with separate routes for some countries.
notes: Students from Canada, Japan, and the U.S. apply through separate national websites.

name: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme
audience: Bachelor's or master's students with a strong computing profile in computer science, math, engineering, physics, or related fields.
notes: Focused on advanced computing projects at CERN; usually around 9 weeks.

name: CERN Technical Studentship
audience: Students from CERN Member or Associate Member States with at least 18 months of undergraduate studies in a technical field.
notes: Technical placements can run several months; citizenship is tied to CERN Member/Associate Member States.

name: CERN Administrative Studentship
audience: Students from CERN Member or Associate Member States in administrative fields such as business, HR, law, communications, finance, or logistics.
notes: Good non-STEM CERN option for business, law, communications, HR, finance, translation, and logistics students.

name: Amgen Scholars Program
audience: Undergraduates apply to participating host institutions for biomedical or related research; eligibility and deadlines vary by region/site.
notes: Site-specific deadlines and eligibility; applicants should check the regional program and host university rules.

name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program
sponsor: Asian Development Bank / Government of Japan
audience: Nationals of ADB borrowing member countries admitted to approved master's programs at designated institutions; usually under age 35.
notes: Apply through participating institutions; candidates must agree to return home after study.

name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program
audience: Mid-career professionals from developing countries and Japan pursuing development-related master's programs.
notes: Application windows and nomination rules vary by eligible/partner master's program.

name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship
sponsor: Government of Ireland / Higher Education Authority
audience: Non-EU/EEA/Switzerland/UK students applying for one year of full-time NFQ Level 9 or 10 study in Ireland.
notes: Requires an offer from an eligible Irish higher education institution; award includes stipend plus full fee waiver.

name: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships
sponsor: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
audience: Citizens of eligible developing countries; postgraduate applicants need relevant work experience and commitment to home-country development.
notes: Eligibility, subjects, and openings are country-specific; scholars generally commit to contribute to home-country development after study.

name: Australia Awards Scholarships
sponsor: Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
audience: Citizens of participating developing countries, especially Indo-Pacific partner countries; country-specific eligibility and priority sectors apply.
notes: Country pages control opening/closing dates; scholars must leave Australia for at least two years after completing the award.

name: Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals
audience: Citizens of eligible countries applying to eligible full-time Swedish master's programs; leadership and work experience expected.
notes: Applicants must also apply separately to Swedish master's programs through University Admissions.

name: VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarships
audience: Nationals/residents of 29 eligible countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America applying to eligible English-taught ICP programs.
notes: Deadlines can vary by specific program even when the general call deadline is listed.

name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
audience: Graduates from developing countries applying to selected development-related postgraduate courses; practical professional experience is usually required.
notes: Course-specific deadlines and requirements; many EPOS courses expect at least two years of professional experience.

name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
sponsor: Swiss Confederation / Federal Commission for Scholarships
audience: Early-career foreign researchers with master's/PhD or artists from eligible countries; research scholarships require a Swiss academic supervisor.
notes: No bachelor's/master's taught-degree scholarships except limited art scholarships; research applicants need Swiss host-supervisor support.

name: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship
sponsor: Government of Hungary / Tempus Public Foundation
audience: Applicants from eligible sending partner countries apply through the central portal and usually need partner nomination.
notes: Requires sending-partner nomination; university entrance exams/interviews may follow nomination.

name: Türkiye Scholarships
audience: International applicants for full-degree study in Türkiye; eligibility and age limits vary by level.
notes: Often includes Turkish language training; verify annual calendar on the official portal.

name: Romanian Government MFA Scholarships
audience: Foreign citizens from non-EU countries; medicine, dental medicine, and pharmacy excluded.
notes: Hosted in Romania; bachelor's and master's programs are generally in Romanian with a preparatory language year.

name: Study in Canada Scholarships
audience: Students from eligible countries apply for short-term study or research exchanges at Canadian institutions through institutional partnerships.
notes: Hosted in Canada; students generally do not apply independently and must be routed through home/host institutions.

name: Emerging Leaders in the Americas Program (ELAP)
audience: Students from eligible Latin America and Caribbean countries complete short-term exchange study or research at Canadian institutions.
notes: Hosted in Canada; applications are submitted by Canadian institutions, not directly by students.

name: LeadNext: Ambassadors for a Global Future
citizenshipRaw: U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident, Citizen of Eligible Country
audience: Ages 18-25 from the U.S. or eligible Asia-Pacific countries; English fluency and full program availability required.

name: McCall MacBain Scholarship
audience: Applicants to eligible McGill master's or professional programs; leadership, character, community engagement, and academic strength emphasized.

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
audience: Applicants from any country must apply separately to Knight-Hennessy and to a full-time Stanford graduate degree program.

name: Obama Foundation Scholars Program
sponsor: Obama Foundation / Columbia University / University of Chicago
audience: Rising leaders with proven commitment to service and significant work in their communities; full-time academic-year participation required.

name: TechGirls
sponsor: U.S. Department of State / Legacy International
audience: Girls ages 15-17 from eligible countries/regions with strong interest in technology, engineering, or math; one semester of secondary school must remain.

name: TechWomen
